items.stem: In Cypher, why use MERGE instead of CREATE when importing a node that may already exist?

options.text: MERGE matches an existing node with the given pattern or creates it if none is found, avoiding duplicates
options.rationale: Correct: MERGE is get-or-create, so repeated imports do not duplicate the node.

options.text: MERGE always deletes the node first and recreates it
options.rationale: MERGE does not delete; it matches or creates.

options.text: MERGE runs faster because it skips indexes
options.rationale: MERGE benefits from indexes; it does not skip them.

options.text: MERGE can only be used on relationships, not nodes
options.rationale: MERGE works on both nodes and relationships.

items.explanation: Correct: MERGE is get-or-create, so repeated imports do not duplicate the node.

items.stem: Which statements about property-graph modelling in Neo4j are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: Both nodes and relationships can carry properties
options.rationale: Correct: properties can be stored on nodes and on relationships.

options.text: Relationships are first-class and are traversed without computing joins at query time
options.rationale: Correct: relationships are stored directly, so traversals avoid relational-style joins.

options.text: A relationship can exist without connecting any nodes
options.rationale: A relationship always connects a start and an end node.

options.text: Labels and relationship types are interchangeable
options.rationale: Labels classify nodes; relationship types classify relationships; they are not interchangeable.

items.explanation: Correct: properties can be stored on nodes and on relationships.; Correct: relationships are stored directly, so traversals avoid relational-style joins.

items.stem: A variable-length pattern like (a)-[*]->(b) is running extremely slowly. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: The path length is unbounded, so the traversal explores an exponentially large number of paths
options.rationale: Correct: an unbounded variable-length path can blow up combinatorially; bounding the depth controls it.

options.text: Cypher does not support variable-length paths
options.rationale: Cypher does support them; the problem is the missing bound.

options.text: RETURN clauses always make queries slow
options.rationale: RETURN itself is not the bottleneck here.

options.text: MERGE is implicitly being called on every node
options.rationale: No MERGE is involved in a MATCH traversal.

items.explanation: Correct: an unbounded variable-length path can blow up combinatorially; bounding the depth controls it.
